gaps.sentence: You ___ have seen a ghost — there is no such thing!
gaps.hint: a past claim rejected as impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' rejects a past claim as impossible: can't have seen.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well tell him the truth — he will find out anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests doing something because there is no reason not to: might as well.

gaps.sentence: Nobody ___ have predicted that result — it shocked everyone.
gaps.hint: it was impossible at that time
gaps.explanation: 'Could have' in negatives means it was not possible: could have predicted.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay at home tonight, if that is all right.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference: would rather stay.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have booked — the hotel had plenty of rooms left.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' shows an unnecessary completed action: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have seen her face when she heard the news!
gaps.explanation: 'Should have seen' emphasizes how remarkable something was: should have.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have rushed the final checks — now there are errors everywhere.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' criticizes a past action with bad results: shouldn't have rushed.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have received your email — her inbox was full last week.
gaps.hint: ruled out as a past possibility
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' plus the participle rules out a past possibility: can't have received.
